svg.title: The learning rate has a hard ceiling
svg.desc: A whiteboard sketch showing the same parabola four times with a ball descending it - crawling when the learning rate is far below two over L, landing in a few steps near one over L, bouncing between two points forever at exactly two over L, and flying apart above it with that panel crossed out in red - with the stability condition lr less than two over L circled; a contour map of a narrow Rosenbrock valley where plain gradient descent zig-zags across the walls in red while Adam walks down the floor in green; a results table showing gradient descent, momentum, Nesterov and RMSProp never reaching a loss below one thousandth in five thousand steps while Adam does at step 3051; and a stacked bar chart of the 107.84 gigabytes a seven-billion-parameter full fine-tune needs beside a 3.50 gigabyte QLoRA bar.
svg.text: The learning rate has a hard ceiling
the SAME parabola, four learning rates
L = the biggest curvature = the largest eigenvalue of the Hessian
a valley that is narrow one way and flat the other
plain GD zig-zags across the walls
the optimizer is not a detail here.
It decided whether this trained at all.
and what Adam actually costs you: one 7B model, fp16
31x less. This is why LoRA exists.
REMEMBER where the gradient has been.
Adam's state is bigger than the
